### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via getEffectiveObjectPermissions (symbol, a method of class SecurityPlugin))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 80 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **59** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a91409c42e67e9a1c417b8f2efa82c356903a19e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8b0d891a90f2686ea325dd583d5508f1fd597776` — the merge of head `f994c4bcae2ff346056e57c441c40112b500d99d` into base `a91409c42e67e9a1c417b8f2efa82c356903a19e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8b0d891a90f2686ea325dd583d5508f1fd597776 && git checkout 8b0d891a90f2686ea325dd583d5508f1fd597776
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a91409c42e67e9a1c417b8f2efa82c356903a19e f994c4bcae2ff346056e57c441c40112b500d99d && git checkout -B drift-repro a91409c42e67e9a1c417b8f2efa82c356903a19e && git merge --no-ff f994c4bcae2ff346056e57c441c40112b500d99d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a91409c42e67e9a1c417b8f2efa82c356903a19e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a91409c42e67e9a1c417b8f2efa82c356903a19e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `f994c4bcae2ff346056e57c441c40112b500d99d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/engine-registration.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/core/src/security/effective-object-permissions.ts, packages/core/src/security/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints.ts, .changeset/30370-external-read-only-effective-permissions.md

Face: declaration (`Clause-②: yes (widening)` line-initial on the PR body and the changeset). No published schema, no governed path, no narrowing of an authorable surface, so the lane seat records this review at `TIER_DEFAULT`. Reads: the full diff (11 files, +391 −27), card #30370 and its triage 6654015112, claim 6654819469, os-dev report 6655769782.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **One verdict.** `externalWriteGateClosure` is Gate 3 (ADR-0015 §5.3) judged once; `assertWriteAllowed` throws on it with the same message fields as before, and the new public `ObjectQL#isExternalWriteForbidden` answers `!== null` on it. The refusal path is a pure extraction (same early returns: no/`default` datasource, no definition, managed or absent `schemaMode`; closed unless both opt-ins), so the gate's behaviour is unchanged and the map cannot disagree with it. The facade member is a delegation-only stub beside `assertWriteAllowed`'s.
2. **The map.** After the super-user seed (every registered object gets an entry when a wildcard grants super-read, so the card's administrator case is covered), the wildcard fold and the managed clamp, `clampExternalReadOnlyWrites` sets `allowCreate`/`allowEdit`/`allowDelete`/`allowTransfer` false and lowers `modifyAllRecords` to `viewAllRecords` (needed: `objectPermissionGrants` answers edit/delete/transfer on `modifyAllRecords` alone; the read half is kept). The verdicts are computed in full before any clamp, a throwing predicate is logged and clamps nothing, and the annotation reads the same set, never a second asking.
3. **`apiOperations`.** On a closed gate the served set drops `create`, `update`, `delete`, `upsert`, `bulk`, `import`, `restore`, `purge`; read operations and `export` stay. Such an object is always annotated (served < closure), so the console's default-allow path cannot offer a write. No `ui/**` change, as the card expected.
4. **Both builders move together.** `/auth/me/permissions` and `ISecurityService.getEffectiveObjectPermissions` hand over `engineExternalWriteForbidden(ql)`, which asks the engine's member when present and forbids nothing otherwise, so a caller with neither gets the old map. Stated side effect: `current_user.can(obj, 'create'|'edit'|'delete'|'transfer')` answers false on such an object, as the write always did.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server` `patch`: AGENTS.md step 3, a non-protocol widening (new `ObjectQL#isExternalWriteForbidden`, new export `engineExternalWriteForbidden`, new optional accessor and optional third parameter) ships `patch`; `Metadata-protocol: none`. The served map now grants less on a read-only external object, but only what the data plane already refused for every caller, so nothing a caller could do before is removed. No BREAKING banner owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- File surface: one file beyond the claim, `packages/core/src/security/index.ts` (the one export line), noted in the report. Accepted.
- `engine.ts`: #30053 slice 2 (PR #30415) edits private docblocks in the same file; the stub sits beside `assertWriteAllowed`'s, which slice 2 does not move. Whichever lands second merges `main`.
- The dev's unfiled observation (the managed clamp leaves an explicit `modifyAllRecords` able to write) is in the PR's Acceptance notes; the seat files it as a card after landing.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-q2mcix`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CbPxYq1wQmUNWvMZkC`

**VERDICT: PASS**
